>         uid=5_93 StaticText "$"
>         uid=5_94 StaticText "{"
>         uid=5_95 StaticText "mohammad.r.haghighat"
>         uid=5_96 StaticText "}"
>         uid=5_97 StaticText "@intel.com"
>         uid=5_98 StaticText "University of California, Irvine"
>         uid=5_99 StaticText "+"
>         uid=5_100 StaticText "{"
>         uid=5_101 StaticText "mbebenit,changm,franz"
>         uid=5_102 StaticText "}"
>         uid=5_103 StaticText "@uci.edu"
>         uid=5_104 StaticText "Abstract"
>         uid=5_105 StaticText "Dynamic languages such as JavaScript are more difficult to com-"
>         uid=5_106 StaticText "pile than statically typed ones. Since no concrete type information"
>         uid=5_107 StaticText "is available, traditional compilers need to emit generic code that can"
>         uid=5_108 StaticText "handle all possible type combinations at runtime. We present an al-"
>         uid=5_109 StaticText "ternative compilation technique for dynamically-typed languages"
>         uid=5_110 StaticText "that identifies frequently executed loop traces at run-time and then"
>         uid=5_111 StaticText "generates machine code on the fly that is specialized for the ac-"
>         uid=5_112 StaticText "tual dynamic types occurring on each path through the loop. Our"
>         uid=5_113 StaticText "method provides cheap inter-procedural type specialization, and an"
>         uid=5_114 StaticText "elegant and efficient way of incrementally compiling lazily discov-"
>         uid=5_115 StaticText "ered alternative paths through nested loops. We have implemented"
>         uid=5_116 StaticText "a dynamic compiler for JavaScript based on our technique and we"
>         uid=5_117 StaticText "have measured speedups of 10x and more for certain benchmark"
>         uid=5_118 StaticText "programs."
>         uid=5_119 StaticText "Categories and Subject Descriptors"
>         uid=5_120 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_121 StaticText "D.3.4 ["
>         uid=5_122 StaticText "Programming Lan-"
>         uid=5_123 StaticText "guages"
>         uid=5_124 StaticText "]: Processors —"
>         uid=5_125 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_126 StaticText "Incremental compilers, code generation"
>         uid=5_127 StaticText "."
>         uid=5_128 StaticText "General Terms"
>         uid=5_129 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_130 StaticText "Design, Experimentation, Measurement, Perfor-"
>         uid=5_131 StaticText "mance."
>         uid=5_132 StaticText "Keywords"
>         uid=5_133 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_134 StaticText "JavaScript, just-in-time compilation, trace trees."
>         uid=5_135 StaticText "1."
>         uid=5_136 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_137 StaticText "Introduction"
>         uid=5_138 StaticText "Dynamic languages"
>         uid=5_139 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_140 StaticText "such as JavaScript, Python, and Ruby, are pop-"
>         uid=5_141 StaticText "ular since they are expressive, accessible to non-experts, and make"
>         uid=5_142 StaticText "deployment as easy as distributing a source file. They are used for"
>         uid=5_143 StaticText "small scripts as well as for complex applications. JavaScript, for"
>         uid=5_144 StaticText "example, is the de facto standard for client-side web programming"
>         uid=5_145 StaticText "Permission to make digital or hard copies of all or part of this work for personal or"
>         uid=5_146 StaticText "classroom use is granted without fee provided that copies are not made or distributed"
>         uid=5_147 StaticText "for profit or commercial advantage and that copies bear this notice and the full citation"
>         uid=5_148 StaticText "on the first page. To copy otherwise, to republish, to post on servers or to redistribute"
>         uid=5_149 StaticText "to lists, requires prior specific permission and/or a fee."
>         uid=5_150 StaticText "PLDI’09,"
>         uid=5_151 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_152 StaticText "June 15–20, 2009, Dublin, Ireland."
>         uid=5_153 StaticText "Copyright c"
>         uid=5_154 StaticText "©"
>         uid=5_155 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_156 StaticText "2009 ACM 978-1-60558-392-1/09/06. . . $5.00"
>         uid=5_157 StaticText "and is used for the application logic of browser-based productivity"
>         uid=5_158 StaticText "applications such as Google Mail, Google Docs and Zimbra Col-"
>         uid=5_159 StaticText "laboration Suite. In this domain, in order to provide a fluid user"
>         uid=5_160 StaticText "experience and enable a new generation of applications, virtual ma-"
>         uid=5_161 StaticText "chines must provide a low startup time and high performance."
>         uid=5_162 StaticText "Compilers for statically typed languages rely on type informa-"
>         uid=5_163 StaticText "tion to generate efficient machine code. In a dynamically typed pro-"
>         uid=5_164 StaticText "gramming language such as JavaScript, the types of expressions"
>         uid=5_165 StaticText "may vary at runtime. This means that the compiler can no longer"
>         uid=5_166 StaticText "easily transform operations into machine instructions that operate"
>         uid=5_167 StaticText "on one specific type. Without exact type information, the compiler"
>         uid=5_168 StaticText "must emit slower generalized machine code that can deal with all"
>         uid=5_169 StaticText "potential type combinations. While compile-time static type infer-"
>         uid=5_170 StaticText "ence might be able to gather type information to generate opti-"
>         uid=5_171 StaticText "mized machine code, traditional static analysis is very expensive"
>         uid=5_172 StaticText "and hence not well suited for the highly interactive environment of"
>         uid=5_173 StaticText "a web browser."
>         uid=5_174 StaticText "We present a trace-based compilation technique for dynamic"
>         uid=5_175 StaticText "languages that reconciles speed of compilation with excellent per-"
>         uid=5_176 StaticText "formance of the generated machine code. Our system uses a mixed-"
>         uid=5_177 StaticText "mode execution approach: the system starts running JavaScript in a"
>         uid=5_178 StaticText "fast-starting bytecode interpreter. As the program runs, the system"
>         uid=5_179 StaticText "identifies"
>         uid=5_180 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_181 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=5_182 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_183 StaticText "(frequently executed) bytecode sequences, records"
>         uid=5_184 StaticText "them, and compiles them to fast native code. We call such a se-"
>         uid=5_185 StaticText "quence of instructions a"
>         uid=5_186 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_187 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=5_188 StaticText "."
>         uid=5_189 StaticText "Unlike method-based dynamic compilers, our dynamic com-"
>         uid=5_190 StaticText "piler operates at the granularity of individual loops. This design"
>         uid=5_191 StaticText "choice is based on the expectation that programs spend most of"
>         uid=5_192 StaticText "their time in hot loops. Even in dynamically typed languages, we"
>         uid=5_193 StaticText "expect hot loops to be mostly"
>         uid=5_194 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_195 StaticText "type-stable"
>         uid=5_196 StaticText ", meaning that the types of"
>         uid=5_197 StaticText "values are invariant. (12) For example, we would expect loop coun-"
>         uid=5_198 StaticText "ters that start as integers to remain integers for all iterations. When"
>         uid=5_199 StaticText "both of these expectations hold, a trace-based compiler can cover"
>         uid=5_200 StaticText "the program execution with a small number of type-specialized, ef-"
>         uid=5_201 StaticText "ficiently compiled traces."
>         uid=5_202 StaticText "Each compiled trace covers one path through the program with"
>         uid=5_203 StaticText "one mapping of values to types. When the VM executes a compiled"
>         uid=5_204 StaticText "trace, it cannot guarantee that the same path will be followed"
>         uid=5_205 StaticText "or that the same types will occur in subsequent loop iterations."
>         uid=5_206 StaticText "Hence, recording and compiling a trace"
>         uid=5_207 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_208 StaticText "speculates"
>         uid=5_209 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_210 StaticText "that the path and"
>         uid=5_211 StaticText "typing will be exactly as they were during recording for subsequent"
>         uid=5_212 StaticText "iterations of the loop."
>         uid=5_213 StaticText "Every compiled trace contains all the"
>         uid=5_214 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_215 StaticText "guards"
>         uid=5_216 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_217 StaticText "(checks) required"
>         uid=5_218 StaticText "to validate the speculation. If one of the guards fails (if control"
>         uid=5_219 StaticText "flow is different, or a value of a different type is generated), the"
>         uid=5_220 StaticText "trace exits. If an exit becomes hot, the VM can record a"
>         uid=5_221 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_222 StaticText "branch"
>         uid=5_223 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=5_224 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_225 StaticText "starting at the exit to cover the new path. In this way, the VM"
>         uid=5_226 StaticText "records a"
>         uid=5_227 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_228 StaticText "trace tree"
>         uid=5_229 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_230 StaticText "covering all the hot paths through the loop."
>         uid=5_231 StaticText "Nested loops can be difficult to optimize for tracing VMs. In"
>         uid=5_232 StaticText "a na¨"
>         uid=5_233 StaticText "ıve implementation, inner loops would become hot first, and"
>         uid=5_234 StaticText "the VM would start tracing there. When the inner loop exits, the"
>         uid=5_235 StaticText "VM would detect that a different branch was taken. The VM would"
>         uid=5_236 StaticText "try to record a branch trace, and find that the trace reaches not the"
>         uid=5_237 StaticText "inner loop header, but the outer loop header. At this point, the VM"
>         uid=5_238 StaticText "could continue tracing until it reaches the inner loop header again,"
>         uid=5_239 StaticText "thus tracing the outer loop inside a trace tree for the inner loop."
>         uid=5_240 StaticText "But this requires tracing a copy of the outer loop for every side exit"
>         uid=5_241 StaticText "and type combination in the inner loop. In essence, this is a form"
>         uid=5_242 StaticText "of unintended tail duplication, which can easily overflow the code"
>         uid=5_243 StaticText "cache. Alternatively, the VM could simply stop tracing, and give up"
>         uid=5_244 StaticText "on ever tracing outer loops."
>         uid=5_245 StaticText "We solve the nested loop problem by recording"
>         uid=5_246 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_247 StaticText "nested trace"
>         uid=5_248 StaticText "trees"
>         uid=5_249 StaticText ". Our system traces the inner loop exactly as the na¨"
>         uid=5_250 StaticText "ıve version."
>         uid=5_251 StaticText "The system stops extending the inner tree when it reaches an outer"
>         uid=5_252 StaticText "loop, but then it starts a new trace at the outer loop header. When"
>         uid=5_253 StaticText "the outer loop reaches the inner loop header, the system tries to call"
>         uid=5_254 StaticText "the trace tree for the inner loop. If the call succeeds, the VM records"
>         uid=5_255 StaticText "the call to the inner tree as part of the outer trace and finishes"
>         uid=5_256 StaticText "the outer trace as normal. In this way, our system can trace any"
>         uid=5_257 StaticText "number of loops nested to any depth without causing excessive tail"
>         uid=5_258 StaticText "duplication."
>         uid=5_259 StaticText "These techniques allow a VM to dynamically translate a pro-"
>         uid=5_260 StaticText "gram to nested, type-specialized trace trees. Because traces can"
>         uid=5_261 StaticText "cross function call boundaries, our techniques also achieve the ef-"
>         uid=5_262 StaticText "fects of inlining. Because traces have no internal control-flow joins,"
>         uid=5_263 StaticText "they can be optimized in linear time by a simple compiler (10)."
>         uid=5_264 StaticText "Thus, our tracing VM efficiently performs the same kind of op-"
>         uid=5_265 StaticText "timizations that would require interprocedural analysis in a static"
>         uid=5_266 StaticText "optimization setting. This makes tracing an attractive and effective"
>         uid=5_267 StaticText "tool to type specialize even complex function call-rich code."
>         uid=5_268 StaticText "We implemented these techniques for an existing JavaScript in-"
>         uid=5_269 StaticText "terpreter, SpiderMonkey. We call the resulting tracing VM"
>         uid=5_270 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_271 StaticText "Trace-"
>         uid=5_272 StaticText "Monkey"
>         uid=5_273 StaticText ". TraceMonkey supports all the JavaScript features of Spi-"
>         uid=5_274 StaticText "derMonkey, with a 2x-20x speedup for traceable programs."
>         uid=5_275 StaticText "This paper makes the following contributions:"
>         uid=5_276 StaticText "•"
>         uid=5_277 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_278 StaticText "We explain an algorithm for dynamically forming trace trees to"
>         uid=5_279 StaticText "cover a program, representing nested loops as nested trace trees."
>         uid=5_280 StaticText "•"
>         uid=5_281 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_282 StaticText "We explain how to speculatively generate efficient type-specialized"
>         uid=5_283 StaticText "code for traces from dynamic language programs."
>         uid=5_284 StaticText "•"
>         uid=5_285 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_286 StaticText "We validate our tracing techniques in an implementation based"
>         uid=5_287 StaticText "on the SpiderMonkey JavaScript interpreter, achieving 2x-20x"
>         uid=5_288 StaticText "speedups on many programs."
>         uid=5_289 StaticText "The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 3 is"
>         uid=5_290 StaticText "a general overview of trace tree based compilation we use to cap-"
>         uid=5_291 StaticText "ture and compile frequently executed code regions. In Section 4"
>         uid=5_292 StaticText "we describe our approach of covering nested loops using a num-"
>         uid=5_293 StaticText "ber of individual trace trees. In Section 5 we describe our trace-"
>         uid=5_294 StaticText "compilation based speculative type specialization approach we use"
>         uid=5_295 StaticText "to generate efficient machine code from recorded bytecode traces."
>         uid=5_296 StaticText "Our implementation of a dynamic type-specializing compiler for"
>         uid=5_297 StaticText "JavaScript is described in Section 6. Related work is discussed in"
>         uid=5_298 StaticText "Section 8. In Section 7 we evaluate our dynamic compiler based on"
>         uid=5_299 StaticText "1 for (var i = 2; i < 100; ++i) {"
>         uid=5_300 StaticText "2"
>         uid=5_301 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_302 StaticText "if (!primes[i])"
>         uid=5_303 StaticText "3"
>         uid=5_304 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_305 StaticText "continue;"
>         uid=5_306 StaticText "4"
>         uid=5_307 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_308 StaticText "for (var k = i + i; i < 100; k += i)"
>         uid=5_309 StaticText "5"
>         uid=5_310 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_311 StaticText "primes[k] = false;"
>         uid=5_312 StaticText "6 }"
>         uid=5_313 StaticText "Figure 1. Sample program: sieve of Eratosthenes."
>         uid=5_314 StaticText " "

>         uid=5_360 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_361 StaticText "State machine describing the major activities of Trace-"
>         uid=5_362 StaticText "Monkey and the conditions that cause transitions to a new activ-"
>         uid=5_363 StaticText "ity. In the dark box, TM executes JS as compiled traces. In the"
>         uid=5_364 StaticText "light gray boxes, TM executes JS in the standard interpreter. White"
>         uid=5_365 StaticText "boxes are overhead. Thus, to maximize performance, we need to"
>         uid=5_366 StaticText "maximize time spent in the darkest box and minimize time spent in"
>         uid=5_367 StaticText "the white boxes. The best case is a loop where the types at the loop"
>         uid=5_368 StaticText "edge are the same as the types on entry–then TM can stay in native"
>         uid=5_369 StaticText "code until the loop is done."
>         uid=5_370 StaticText "a set of industry benchmarks. The paper ends with conclusions in"
>         uid=5_371 StaticText "Section 9 and an outlook on future work is presented in Section 10."
>         uid=5_372 StaticText "2."
>         uid=5_373 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_374 StaticText "Overview: Example Tracing Run"
>         uid=5_375 StaticText "This section provides an overview of our system by describing"
>         uid=5_376 StaticText "how TraceMonkey executes an example program. The example"
>         uid=5_377 StaticText "program, shown in Figure 1, computes the first 100 prime numbers"
>         uid=5_378 StaticText "with nested loops. The narrative should be read along with Figure 2,"
>         uid=5_379 StaticText "which describes the activities TraceMonkey performs and when it"
>         uid=5_380 StaticText "transitions between the loops."
>         uid=5_381 StaticText "TraceMonkey always begins executing a program in the byte-"
>         uid=5_382 StaticText "code interpreter. Every loop back edge is a potential trace point."
>         uid=5_383 StaticText "When the interpreter crosses a loop edge, TraceMonkey invokes"
>         uid=5_384 StaticText "the"
>         uid=5_385 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_386 StaticText "trace monitor"
>         uid=5_387 StaticText ", which may decide to record or execute a native"
>         uid=5_388 StaticText "trace. At the start of execution, there are no compiled traces yet, so"
>         uid=5_389 StaticText "the trace monitor counts the number of times each loop back edge is"
>         uid=5_390 StaticText "executed until a loop becomes"
>         uid=5_391 StaticText " "
>         uid=5_392 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=5_393 StaticText ", currently after 2 crossings. Note"
>         uid=5_394 StaticText "that the way our loops are compiled, the loop edge is crossed before"
>         uid=5_395 StaticText "entering the loop, so the second crossing occurs immediately after"
>         uid=5_396 StaticText "the first iteration."
>         uid=5_397 StaticText "Here is the sequence of events broken down by outer loop"
>         uid=5_398 StaticText "iteration:"

>         uid=8_44 StaticText "Languages"

>         uid=8_59 StaticText ", Blake Kaplan"

>         uid=8_62 StaticText "∗"

>         uid=8_65 StaticText ", Jason Orendorff"

>         uid=8_69 StaticText "∗"

>         uid=8_71 StaticText "#"

>         uid=8_73 StaticText "#"
>         uid=8_74 StaticText ", Michael Bebenita"

>         uid=8_80 StaticText "Mozilla Corporation"

>         uid=8_83 StaticText "gal,brendan,shaver,danderson,dmandelin,mrbkap,graydon,bz,jorendorff,jruderman"
>         uid=8_84 StaticText "}"
>         uid=8_85 StaticText "@mozilla.com"
>         uid=8_86 StaticText "Adobe Corporation"

>         uid=8_89 StaticText "edwsmith,rreitmai"
>         uid=8_90 StaticText "}"
>         uid=8_91 StaticText "@adobe.com"
>         uid=8_92 StaticText "Intel Corporation"
>         uid=8_93 StaticText "$"
>         uid=8_94 StaticText "{"
>         uid=8_95 StaticText "mohammad.r.haghighat"
>         uid=8_96 StaticText "}"
>         uid=8_97 StaticText "@intel.com"
>         uid=8_98 StaticText "University of California, Irvine"
>         uid=8_99 StaticText "+"
>         uid=8_100 StaticText "{"
>         uid=8_101 StaticText "mbebenit,changm,franz"
>         uid=8_102 StaticText "}"
>         uid=8_103 StaticText "@uci.edu"
>         uid=8_104 StaticText "Abstract"
>         uid=8_105 StaticText "Dynamic languages such as JavaScript are more difficult to com-"
>         uid=8_106 StaticText "pile than statically typed ones. Since no concrete type information"
>         uid=8_107 StaticText "is available, traditional compilers need to emit generic code that can"
>         uid=8_108 StaticText "handle all possible type combinations at runtime. We present an al-"
>         uid=8_109 StaticText "ternative compilation technique for dynamically-typed languages"
>         uid=8_110 StaticText "that identifies frequently executed loop traces at run-time and then"
>         uid=8_111 StaticText "generates machine code on the fly that is specialized for the ac-"
>         uid=8_112 StaticText "tual dynamic types occurring on each path through the loop. Our"
>         uid=8_113 StaticText "method provides cheap inter-procedural type specialization, and an"
>         uid=8_114 StaticText "elegant and efficient way of incrementally compiling lazily discov-"
>         uid=8_115 StaticText "ered alternative paths through nested loops. We have implemented"
>         uid=8_116 StaticText "a dynamic compiler for JavaScript based on our technique and we"
>         uid=8_117 StaticText "have measured speedups of 10x and more for certain benchmark"
>         uid=8_118 StaticText "programs."
>         uid=8_119 StaticText "Categories and Subject Descriptors"
>         uid=8_120 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_121 StaticText "D.3.4 ["
>         uid=8_122 StaticText "Programming Lan-"
>         uid=8_123 StaticText "guages"
>         uid=8_124 StaticText "]: Processors —"
>         uid=8_125 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_126 StaticText "Incremental compilers, code generation"
>         uid=8_127 StaticText "."
>         uid=8_128 StaticText "General Terms"
>         uid=8_129 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_130 StaticText "Design, Experimentation, Measurement, Perfor-"
>         uid=8_131 StaticText "mance."
>         uid=8_132 StaticText "Keywords"
>         uid=8_133 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_134 StaticText "JavaScript, just-in-time compilation, trace trees."
>         uid=8_135 StaticText "1."
>         uid=8_136 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_137 StaticText "Introduction"
>         uid=8_138 StaticText "Dynamic languages"
>         uid=8_139 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_140 StaticText "such as JavaScript, Python, and Ruby, are pop-"
>         uid=8_141 StaticText "ular since they are expressive, accessible to non-experts, and make"
>         uid=8_142 StaticText "deployment as easy as distributing a source file. They are used for"
>         uid=8_143 StaticText "small scripts as well as for complex applications. JavaScript, for"
>         uid=8_144 StaticText "example, is the de facto standard for client-side web programming"
>         uid=8_145 StaticText "Permission to make digital or hard copies of all or part of this work for personal or"
>         uid=8_146 StaticText "classroom use is granted without fee provided that copies are not made or distributed"
>         uid=8_147 StaticText "for profit or commercial advantage and that copies bear this notice and the full citation"
>         uid=8_148 StaticText "on the first page. To copy otherwise, to republish, to post on servers or to redistribute"
>         uid=8_149 StaticText "to lists, requires prior specific permission and/or a fee."
>         uid=8_150 StaticText "PLDI’09,"
>         uid=8_151 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_152 StaticText "June 15–20, 2009, Dublin, Ireland."
>         uid=8_153 StaticText "Copyright c"
>         uid=8_154 StaticText "©"
>         uid=8_155 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_156 StaticText "2009 ACM 978-1-60558-392-1/09/06. . . $5.00"
>         uid=8_157 StaticText "and is used for the application logic of browser-based productivity"
>         uid=8_158 StaticText "applications such as Google Mail, Google Docs and Zimbra Col-"
>         uid=8_159 StaticText "laboration Suite. In this domain, in order to provide a fluid user"
>         uid=8_160 StaticText "experience and enable a new generation of applications, virtual ma-"
>         uid=8_161 StaticText "chines must provide a low startup time and high performance."
>         uid=8_162 StaticText "Compilers for statically typed languages rely on type informa-"
>         uid=8_163 StaticText "tion to generate efficient machine code. In a dynamically typed pro-"
>         uid=8_164 StaticText "gramming language such as JavaScript, the types of expressions"
>         uid=8_165 StaticText "may vary at runtime. This means that the compiler can no longer"
>         uid=8_166 StaticText "easily transform operations into machine instructions that operate"
>         uid=8_167 StaticText "on one specific type. Without exact type information, the compiler"
>         uid=8_168 StaticText "must emit slower generalized machine code that can deal with all"
>         uid=8_169 StaticText "potential type combinations. While compile-time static type infer-"
>         uid=8_170 StaticText "ence might be able to gather type information to generate opti-"
>         uid=8_171 StaticText "mized machine code, traditional static analysis is very expensive"
>         uid=8_172 StaticText "and hence not well suited for the highly interactive environment of"
>         uid=8_173 StaticText "a web browser."
>         uid=8_174 StaticText "We present a trace-based compilation technique for dynamic"
>         uid=8_175 StaticText "languages that reconciles speed of compilation with excellent per-"
>         uid=8_176 StaticText "formance of the generated machine code. Our system uses a mixed-"
>         uid=8_177 StaticText "mode execution approach: the system starts running JavaScript in a"
>         uid=8_178 StaticText "fast-starting bytecode interpreter. As the program runs, the system"
>         uid=8_179 StaticText "identifies"
>         uid=8_180 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_181 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=8_182 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_183 StaticText "(frequently executed) bytecode sequences, records"
>         uid=8_184 StaticText "them, and compiles them to fast native code. We call such a se-"
>         uid=8_185 StaticText "quence of instructions a"
>         uid=8_186 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_187 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=8_188 StaticText "."
>         uid=8_189 StaticText "Unlike method-based dynamic compilers, our dynamic com-"
>         uid=8_190 StaticText "piler operates at the granularity of individual loops. This design"
>         uid=8_191 StaticText "choice is based on the expectation that programs spend most of"
>         uid=8_192 StaticText "their time in hot loops. Even in dynamically typed languages, we"
>         uid=8_193 StaticText "expect hot loops to be mostly"
>         uid=8_194 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_195 StaticText "type-stable"
>         uid=8_196 StaticText ", meaning that the types of"
>         uid=8_197 StaticText "values are invariant. (12) For example, we would expect loop coun-"
>         uid=8_198 StaticText "ters that start as integers to remain integers for all iterations. When"
>         uid=8_199 StaticText "both of these expectations hold, a trace-based compiler can cover"
>         uid=8_200 StaticText "the program execution with a small number of type-specialized, ef-"
>         uid=8_201 StaticText "ficiently compiled traces."
>         uid=8_202 StaticText "Each compiled trace covers one path through the program with"
>         uid=8_203 StaticText "one mapping of values to types. When the VM executes a compiled"
>         uid=8_204 StaticText "trace, it cannot guarantee that the same path will be followed"
>         uid=8_205 StaticText "or that the same types will occur in subsequent loop iterations."
>         uid=8_206 StaticText "Hence, recording and compiling a trace"
>         uid=8_207 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_208 StaticText "speculates"
>         uid=8_209 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_210 StaticText "that the path and"
>         uid=8_211 StaticText "typing will be exactly as they were during recording for subsequent"
>         uid=8_212 StaticText "iterations of the loop."
>         uid=8_213 StaticText "Every compiled trace contains all the"
>         uid=8_214 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_215 StaticText "guards"
>         uid=8_216 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_217 StaticText "(checks) required"
>         uid=8_218 StaticText "to validate the speculation. If one of the guards fails (if control"
>         uid=8_219 StaticText "flow is different, or a value of a different type is generated), the"
>         uid=8_220 StaticText "trace exits. If an exit becomes hot, the VM can record a"
>         uid=8_221 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_222 StaticText "branch"
>         uid=8_223 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=8_224 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_225 StaticText "starting at the exit to cover the new path. In this way, the VM"
>         uid=8_226 StaticText "records a"
>         uid=8_227 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_228 StaticText "trace tree"
>         uid=8_229 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_230 StaticText "covering all the hot paths through the loop."
>         uid=8_231 StaticText "Nested loops can be difficult to optimize for tracing VMs. In"
>         uid=8_232 StaticText "a na¨"
>         uid=8_233 StaticText "ıve implementation, inner loops would become hot first, and"
>         uid=8_234 StaticText "the VM would start tracing there. When the inner loop exits, the"
>         uid=8_235 StaticText "VM would detect that a different branch was taken. The VM would"
>         uid=8_236 StaticText "try to record a branch trace, and find that the trace reaches not the"
>         uid=8_237 StaticText "inner loop header, but the outer loop header. At this point, the VM"
>         uid=8_238 StaticText "could continue tracing until it reaches the inner loop header again,"
>         uid=8_239 StaticText "thus tracing the outer loop inside a trace tree for the inner loop."
>         uid=8_240 StaticText "But this requires tracing a copy of the outer loop for every side exit"
>         uid=8_241 StaticText "and type combination in the inner loop. In essence, this is a form"
>         uid=8_242 StaticText "of unintended tail duplication, which can easily overflow the code"
>         uid=8_243 StaticText "cache. Alternatively, the VM could simply stop tracing, and give up"
>         uid=8_244 StaticText "on ever tracing outer loops."
>         uid=8_245 StaticText "We solve the nested loop problem by recording"
>         uid=8_246 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_247 StaticText "nested trace"
>         uid=8_248 StaticText "trees"
>         uid=8_249 StaticText ". Our system traces the inner loop exactly as the na¨"
>         uid=8_250 StaticText "ıve version."
>         uid=8_251 StaticText "The system stops extending the inner tree when it reaches an outer"
>         uid=8_252 StaticText "loop, but then it starts a new trace at the outer loop header. When"
>         uid=8_253 StaticText "the outer loop reaches the inner loop header, the system tries to call"
>         uid=8_254 StaticText "the trace tree for the inner loop. If the call succeeds, the VM records"
>         uid=8_255 StaticText "the call to the inner tree as part of the outer trace and finishes"
>         uid=8_256 StaticText "the outer trace as normal. In this way, our system can trace any"
>         uid=8_257 StaticText "number of loops nested to any depth without causing excessive tail"
>         uid=8_258 StaticText "duplication."
>         uid=8_259 StaticText "These techniques allow a VM to dynamically translate a pro-"
>         uid=8_260 StaticText "gram to nested, type-specialized trace trees. Because traces can"
>         uid=8_261 StaticText "cross function call boundaries, our techniques also achieve the ef-"
>         uid=8_262 StaticText "fects of inlining. Because traces have no internal control-flow joins,"
>         uid=8_263 StaticText "they can be optimized in linear time by a simple compiler (10)."
>         uid=8_264 StaticText "Thus, our tracing VM efficiently performs the same kind of op-"
>         uid=8_265 StaticText "timizations that would require interprocedural analysis in a static"
>         uid=8_266 StaticText "optimization setting. This makes tracing an attractive and effective"
>         uid=8_267 StaticText "tool to type specialize even complex function call-rich code."
>         uid=8_268 StaticText "We implemented these techniques for an existing JavaScript in-"
>         uid=8_269 StaticText "terpreter, SpiderMonkey. We call the resulting tracing VM"
>         uid=8_270 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_271 StaticText "Trace-"
>         uid=8_272 StaticText "Monkey"
>         uid=8_273 StaticText ". TraceMonkey supports all the JavaScript features of Spi-"
>         uid=8_274 StaticText "derMonkey, with a 2x-20x speedup for traceable programs."
>         uid=8_275 StaticText "This paper makes the following contributions:"
>         uid=8_276 StaticText "•"
>         uid=8_277 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_278 StaticText "We explain an algorithm for dynamically forming trace trees to"
>         uid=8_279 StaticText "cover a program, representing nested loops as nested trace trees."
>         uid=8_280 StaticText "•"
>         uid=8_281 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_282 StaticText "We explain how to speculatively generate efficient type-specialized"
>         uid=8_283 StaticText "code for traces from dynamic language programs."
>         uid=8_284 StaticText "•"
>         uid=8_285 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_286 StaticText "We validate our tracing techniques in an implementation based"
>         uid=8_287 StaticText "on the SpiderMonkey JavaScript interpreter, achieving 2x-20x"
>         uid=8_288 StaticText "speedups on many programs."
>         uid=8_289 StaticText "The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 3 is"
>         uid=8_290 StaticText "a general overview of trace tree based compilation we use to cap-"
>         uid=8_291 StaticText "ture and compile frequently executed code regions. In Section 4"
>         uid=8_292 StaticText "we describe our approach of covering nested loops using a num-"
>         uid=8_293 StaticText "ber of individual trace trees. In Section 5 we describe our trace-"
>         uid=8_294 StaticText "compilation based speculative type specialization approach we use"
>         uid=8_295 StaticText "to generate efficient machine code from recorded bytecode traces."
>         uid=8_296 StaticText "Our implementation of a dynamic type-specializing compiler for"
>         uid=8_297 StaticText "JavaScript is described in Section 6. Related work is discussed in"
>         uid=8_298 StaticText "Section 8. In Section 7 we evaluate our dynamic compiler based on"
>         uid=8_299 StaticText "1 for (var i = 2; i < 100; ++i) {"
>         uid=8_300 StaticText "2"
>         uid=8_301 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_302 StaticText "if (!primes[i])"
>         uid=8_303 StaticText "3"
>         uid=8_304 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_305 StaticText "continue;"
>         uid=8_306 StaticText "4"
>         uid=8_307 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_308 StaticText "for (var k = i + i; i < 100; k += i)"
>         uid=8_309 StaticText "5"
>         uid=8_310 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_311 StaticText "primes[k] = false;"
>         uid=8_312 StaticText "6 }"
>         uid=8_313 StaticText "Figure 1. Sample program: sieve of Eratosthenes."
>         uid=8_314 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_315 StaticText "primes"
>         uid=8_316 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_317 StaticText "is"
>         uid=8_318 StaticText "initialized to an array of 100"
>         uid=8_319 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_320 StaticText "false"
>         uid=8_321 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_322 StaticText "values on entry to this code"
>         uid=8_323 StaticText "snippet."
>         uid=8_324 StaticText "Interpret"
>         uid=8_325 StaticText "Bytecodes"
>         uid=8_326 StaticText "Monitor"
>         uid=8_327 StaticText "Record"
>         uid=8_328 StaticText "LIR Trace"
>         uid=8_329 StaticText "Execute"
>         uid=8_330 StaticText "Compiled Trace"
>         uid=8_331 StaticText "Enter"
>         uid=8_332 StaticText "Compiled Trace"
>         uid=8_333 StaticText "Compile"
>         uid=8_334 StaticText "LIR Trace"
>         uid=8_335 StaticText "Leave"
>         uid=8_336 StaticText "Compiled Trace"
>         uid=8_337 StaticText "loop"
>         uid=8_338 StaticText "edge"
>         uid=8_339 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=8_340 StaticText "loop/exit"
>         uid=8_341 StaticText "abort"
>         uid=8_342 StaticText "recording"
>         uid=8_343 StaticText "finish at"
>         uid=8_344 StaticText "loop header"
>         uid=8_345 StaticText "cold/blacklisted"
>         uid=8_346 StaticText "loop/exit"
>         uid=8_347 StaticText "compiled trace"
>         uid=8_348 StaticText "ready"
>         uid=8_349 StaticText "loop edge with"
>         uid=8_350 StaticText "same types"
>         uid=8_351 StaticText "side exit to"
>         uid=8_352 StaticText "existing trace"
>         uid=8_353 StaticText "side exit,"
>         uid=8_354 StaticText "no existing trace"
>         uid=8_355 StaticText "Overhead"
>         uid=8_356 StaticText "Interpreting"
>         uid=8_357 StaticText "Native"
>         uid=8_358 StaticText "Symbol Key"
>         uid=8_359 StaticText "Figure 2."
>         uid=8_360 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_361 StaticText "State machine describing the major activities of Trace-"
>         uid=8_362 StaticText "Monkey and the conditions that cause transitions to a new activ-"
>         uid=8_363 StaticText "ity. In the dark box, TM executes JS as compiled traces. In the"
>         uid=8_364 StaticText "light gray boxes, TM executes JS in the standard interpreter. White"
>         uid=8_365 StaticText "boxes are overhead. Thus, to maximize performance, we need to"
>         uid=8_366 StaticText "maximize time spent in the darkest box and minimize time spent in"
>         uid=8_367 StaticText "the white boxes. The best case is a loop where the types at the loop"
>         uid=8_368 StaticText "edge are the same as the types on entry–then TM can stay in native"
>         uid=8_369 StaticText "code until the loop is done."
>         uid=8_370 StaticText "a set of industry benchmarks. The paper ends with conclusions in"
>         uid=8_371 StaticText "Section 9 and an outlook on future work is presented in Section 10."
>         uid=8_372 StaticText "2."
>         uid=8_373 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_374 StaticText "Overview: Example Tracing Run"
>         uid=8_375 StaticText "This section provides an overview of our system by describing"
>         uid=8_376 StaticText "how TraceMonkey executes an example program. The example"
>         uid=8_377 StaticText "program, shown in Figure 1, computes the first 100 prime numbers"
>         uid=8_378 StaticText "with nested loops. The narrative should be read along with Figure 2,"
>         uid=8_379 StaticText "which describes the activities TraceMonkey performs and when it"
>         uid=8_380 StaticText "transitions between the loops."
>         uid=8_381 StaticText "TraceMonkey always begins executing a program in the byte-"
>         uid=8_382 StaticText "code interpreter. Every loop back edge is a potential trace point."
>         uid=8_383 StaticText "When the interpreter crosses a loop edge, TraceMonkey invokes"
>         uid=8_384 StaticText "the"
>         uid=8_385 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_386 StaticText "trace monitor"
>         uid=8_387 StaticText ", which may decide to record or execute a native"
>         uid=8_388 StaticText "trace. At the start of execution, there are no compiled traces yet, so"
>         uid=8_389 StaticText "the trace monitor counts the number of times each loop back edge is"
>         uid=8_390 StaticText "executed until a loop becomes"
>         uid=8_391 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_392 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=8_393 StaticText ", currently after 2 crossings. Note"
>         uid=8_394 StaticText "that the way our loops are compiled, the loop edge is crossed before"
>         uid=8_395 StaticText "entering the loop, so the second crossing occurs immediately after"
>         uid=8_396 StaticText "the first iteration."
>         uid=8_397 StaticText "Here is the sequence of events broken down by outer loop"
>         uid=8_398 StaticText "iteration:"

>         uid=8_65 StaticText ", Jason Orendorff"

>         uid=8_69 StaticText "∗"

>         uid=8_71 StaticText "#"

>         uid=8_73 StaticText "#"
>         uid=8_74 StaticText ", Michael Bebenita"

>         uid=8_83 StaticText "gal,brendan,shaver,danderson,dmandelin,mrbkap,graydon,bz,jorendorff,jruderman"
>         uid=8_84 StaticText "}"

>         uid=8_91 StaticText "@adobe.com"
>         uid=8_92 StaticText "Intel Corporation"
>         uid=8_93 StaticText "$"
>         uid=8_94 StaticText "{"
>         uid=8_95 StaticText "mohammad.r.haghighat"
>         uid=8_96 StaticText "}"
>         uid=8_97 StaticText "@intel.com"
>         uid=8_98 StaticText "University of California, Irvine"
>         uid=8_99 StaticText "+"
>         uid=8_100 StaticText "{"
>         uid=8_101 StaticText "mbebenit,changm,franz"
>         uid=8_102 StaticText "}"
>         uid=8_103 StaticText "@uci.edu"
>         uid=8_104 StaticText "Abstract"
>         uid=8_105 StaticText "Dynamic languages such as JavaScript are more difficult to com-"
>         uid=8_106 StaticText "pile than statically typed ones. Since no concrete type information"
>         uid=8_107 StaticText "is available, traditional compilers need to emit generic code that can"
>         uid=8_108 StaticText "handle all possible type combinations at runtime. We present an al-"
>         uid=8_109 StaticText "ternative compilation technique for dynamically-typed languages"
>         uid=8_110 StaticText "that identifies frequently executed loop traces at run-time and then"
>         uid=8_111 StaticText "generates machine code on the fly that is specialized for the ac-"
>         uid=8_112 StaticText "tual dynamic types occurring on each path through the loop. Our"
>         uid=8_113 StaticText "method provides cheap inter-procedural type specialization, and an"
>         uid=8_114 StaticText "elegant and efficient way of incrementally compiling lazily discov-"
>         uid=8_115 StaticText "ered alternative paths through nested loops. We have implemented"
>         uid=8_116 StaticText "a dynamic compiler for JavaScript based on our technique and we"
>         uid=8_117 StaticText "have measured speedups of 10x and more for certain benchmark"
>         uid=8_118 StaticText "programs."
>         uid=8_119 StaticText "Categories and Subject Descriptors"
>         uid=8_120 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_121 StaticText "D.3.4 ["
>         uid=8_122 StaticText "Programming Lan-"
>         uid=8_123 StaticText "guages"
>         uid=8_124 StaticText "]: Processors —"
>         uid=8_125 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_126 StaticText "Incremental compilers, code generation"
>         uid=8_127 StaticText "."
>         uid=8_128 StaticText "General Terms"
>         uid=8_129 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_130 StaticText "Design, Experimentation, Measurement, Perfor-"
>         uid=8_131 StaticText "mance."
>         uid=8_132 StaticText "Keywords"
>         uid=8_133 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_134 StaticText "JavaScript, just-in-time compilation, trace trees."
>         uid=8_135 StaticText "1."
>         uid=8_136 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_137 StaticText "Introduction"
>         uid=8_138 StaticText "Dynamic languages"
>         uid=8_139 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_140 StaticText "such as JavaScript, Python, and Ruby, are pop-"
>         uid=8_141 StaticText "ular since they are expressive, accessible to non-experts, and make"
>         uid=8_142 StaticText "deployment as easy as distributing a source file. They are used for"
>         uid=8_143 StaticText "small scripts as well as for complex applications. JavaScript, for"
>         uid=8_144 StaticText "example, is the de facto standard for client-side web programming"
>         uid=8_145 StaticText "Permission to make digital or hard copies of all or part of this work for personal or"
>         uid=8_146 StaticText "classroom use is granted without fee provided that copies are not made or distributed"
>         uid=8_147 StaticText "for profit or commercial advantage and that copies bear this notice and the full citation"
>         uid=8_148 StaticText "on the first page. To copy otherwise, to republish, to post on servers or to redistribute"
>         uid=8_149 StaticText "to lists, requires prior specific permission and/or a fee."
>         uid=8_150 StaticText "PLDI’09,"
>         uid=8_151 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_152 StaticText "June 15–20, 2009, Dublin, Ireland."
>         uid=8_153 StaticText "Copyright c"
>         uid=8_154 StaticText "©"
>         uid=8_155 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_156 StaticText "2009 ACM 978-1-60558-392-1/09/06. . . $5.00"
>         uid=8_157 StaticText "and is used for the application logic of browser-based productivity"
>         uid=8_158 StaticText "applications such as Google Mail, Google Docs and Zimbra Col-"
>         uid=8_159 StaticText "laboration Suite. In this domain, in order to provide a fluid user"
>         uid=8_160 StaticText "experience and enable a new generation of applications, virtual ma-"
>         uid=8_161 StaticText "chines must provide a low startup time and high performance."
>         uid=8_162 StaticText "Compilers for statically typed languages rely on type informa-"
>         uid=8_163 StaticText "tion to generate efficient machine code. In a dynamically typed pro-"
>         uid=8_164 StaticText "gramming language such as JavaScript, the types of expressions"
>         uid=8_165 StaticText "may vary at runtime. This means that the compiler can no longer"
>         uid=8_166 StaticText "easily transform operations into machine instructions that operate"
>         uid=8_167 StaticText "on one specific type. Without exact type information, the compiler"
>         uid=8_168 StaticText "must emit slower generalized machine code that can deal with all"
>         uid=8_169 StaticText "potential type combinations. While compile-time static type infer-"
>         uid=8_170 StaticText "ence might be able to gather type information to generate opti-"
>         uid=8_171 StaticText "mized machine code, traditional static analysis is very expensive"
>         uid=8_172 StaticText "and hence not well suited for the highly interactive environment of"
>         uid=8_173 StaticText "a web browser."
>         uid=8_174 StaticText "We present a trace-based compilation technique for dynamic"
>         uid=8_175 StaticText "languages that reconciles speed of compilation with excellent per-"
>         uid=8_176 StaticText "formance of the generated machine code. Our system uses a mixed-"
>         uid=8_177 StaticText "mode execution approach: the system starts running JavaScript in a"
>         uid=8_178 StaticText "fast-starting bytecode interpreter. As the program runs, the system"
>         uid=8_179 StaticText "identifies"
>         uid=8_180 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_181 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=8_182 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_183 StaticText "(frequently executed) bytecode sequences, records"
>         uid=8_184 StaticText "them, and compiles them to fast native code. We call such a se-"
>         uid=8_185 StaticText "quence of instructions a"
>         uid=8_186 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_187 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=8_188 StaticText "."
>         uid=8_189 StaticText "Unlike method-based dynamic compilers, our dynamic com-"
>         uid=8_190 StaticText "piler operates at the granularity of individual loops. This design"
>         uid=8_191 StaticText "choice is based on the expectation that programs spend most of"
>         uid=8_192 StaticText "their time in hot loops. Even in dynamically typed languages, we"
>         uid=8_193 StaticText "expect hot loops to be mostly"
>         uid=8_194 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_195 StaticText "type-stable"
>         uid=8_196 StaticText ", meaning that the types of"
>         uid=8_197 StaticText "values are invariant. (12) For example, we would expect loop coun-"
>         uid=8_198 StaticText "ters that start as integers to remain integers for all iterations. When"
>         uid=8_199 StaticText "both of these expectations hold, a trace-based compiler can cover"
>         uid=8_200 StaticText "the program execution with a small number of type-specialized, ef-"
>         uid=8_201 StaticText "ficiently compiled traces."
>         uid=8_202 StaticText "Each compiled trace covers one path through the program with"
>         uid=8_203 StaticText "one mapping of values to types. When the VM executes a compiled"
>         uid=8_204 StaticText "trace, it cannot guarantee that the same path will be followed"
>         uid=8_205 StaticText "or that the same types will occur in subsequent loop iterations."
>         uid=8_206 StaticText "Hence, recording and compiling a trace"
>         uid=8_207 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_208 StaticText "speculates"
>         uid=8_209 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_210 StaticText "that the path and"
>         uid=8_211 StaticText "typing will be exactly as they were during recording for subsequent"
>         uid=8_212 StaticText "iterations of the loop."
>         uid=8_213 StaticText "Every compiled trace contains all the"
>         uid=8_214 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_215 StaticText "guards"
>         uid=8_216 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_217 StaticText "(checks) required"
>         uid=8_218 StaticText "to validate the speculation. If one of the guards fails (if control"
>         uid=8_219 StaticText "flow is different, or a value of a different type is generated), the"
>         uid=8_220 StaticText "trace exits. If an exit becomes hot, the VM can record a"
>         uid=8_221 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_222 StaticText "branch"
>         uid=8_223 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=8_224 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_225 StaticText "starting at the exit to cover the new path. In this way, the VM"
>         uid=8_226 StaticText "records a"
>         uid=8_227 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_228 StaticText "trace tree"
>         uid=8_229 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_230 StaticText "covering all the hot paths through the loop."
>         uid=8_231 StaticText "Nested loops can be difficult to optimize for tracing VMs. In"
>         uid=8_232 StaticText "a na¨"
>         uid=8_233 StaticText "ıve implementation, inner loops would become hot first, and"
>         uid=8_234 StaticText "the VM would start tracing there. When the inner loop exits, the"
>         uid=8_235 StaticText "VM would detect that a different branch was taken. The VM would"
>         uid=8_236 StaticText "try to record a branch trace, and find that the trace reaches not the"
>         uid=8_237 StaticText "inner loop header, but the outer loop header. At this point, the VM"
>         uid=8_238 StaticText "could continue tracing until it reaches the inner loop header again,"
>         uid=8_239 StaticText "thus tracing the outer loop inside a trace tree for the inner loop."
>         uid=8_240 StaticText "But this requires tracing a copy of the outer loop for every side exit"
>         uid=8_241 StaticText "and type combination in the inner loop. In essence, this is a form"
>         uid=8_242 StaticText "of unintended tail duplication, which can easily overflow the code"
>         uid=8_243 StaticText "cache. Alternatively, the VM could simply stop tracing, and give up"
>         uid=8_244 StaticText "on ever tracing outer loops."
>         uid=8_245 StaticText "We solve the nested loop problem by recording"
>         uid=8_246 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_247 StaticText "nested trace"
>         uid=8_248 StaticText "trees"
>         uid=8_249 StaticText ". Our system traces the inner loop exactly as the na¨"
>         uid=8_250 StaticText "ıve version."
>         uid=8_251 StaticText "The system stops extending the inner tree when it reaches an outer"
>         uid=8_252 StaticText "loop, but then it starts a new trace at the outer loop header. When"
>         uid=8_253 StaticText "the outer loop reaches the inner loop header, the system tries to call"
>         uid=8_254 StaticText "the trace tree for the inner loop. If the call succeeds, the VM records"
>         uid=8_255 StaticText "the call to the inner tree as part of the outer trace and finishes"
>         uid=8_256 StaticText "the outer trace as normal. In this way, our system can trace any"
>         uid=8_257 StaticText "number of loops nested to any depth without causing excessive tail"
>         uid=8_258 StaticText "duplication."
>         uid=8_259 StaticText "These techniques allow a VM to dynamically translate a pro-"
>         uid=8_260 StaticText "gram to nested, type-specialized trace trees. Because traces can"
>         uid=8_261 StaticText "cross function call boundaries, our techniques also achieve the ef-"
>         uid=8_262 StaticText "fects of inlining. Because traces have no internal control-flow joins,"
>         uid=8_263 StaticText "they can be optimized in linear time by a simple compiler (10)."
>         uid=8_264 StaticText "Thus, our tracing VM efficiently performs the same kind of op-"
>         uid=8_265 StaticText "timizations that would require interprocedural analysis in a static"
>         uid=8_266 StaticText "optimization setting. This makes tracing an attractive and effective"
>         uid=8_267 StaticText "tool to type specialize even complex function call-rich code."
>         uid=8_268 StaticText "We implemented these techniques for an existing JavaScript in-"
>         uid=8_269 StaticText "terpreter, SpiderMonkey. We call the resulting tracing VM"
>         uid=8_270 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_271 StaticText "Trace-"
>         uid=8_272 StaticText "Monkey"
>         uid=8_273 StaticText ". TraceMonkey supports all the JavaScript features of Spi-"
>         uid=8_274 StaticText "derMonkey, with a 2x-20x speedup for traceable programs."
>         uid=8_275 StaticText "This paper makes the following contributions:"
>         uid=8_276 StaticText "•"
>         uid=8_277 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_278 StaticText "We explain an algorithm for dynamically forming trace trees to"
>         uid=8_279 StaticText "cover a program, representing nested loops as nested trace trees."
>         uid=8_280 StaticText "•"
>         uid=8_281 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_282 StaticText "We explain how to speculatively generate efficient type-specialized"
>         uid=8_283 StaticText "code for traces from dynamic language programs."
>         uid=8_284 StaticText "•"
>         uid=8_285 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_286 StaticText "We validate our tracing techniques in an implementation based"
>         uid=8_287 StaticText "on the SpiderMonkey JavaScript interpreter, achieving 2x-20x"
>         uid=8_288 StaticText "speedups on many programs."
>         uid=8_289 StaticText "The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 3 is"
>         uid=8_290 StaticText "a general overview of trace tree based compilation we use to cap-"
>         uid=8_291 StaticText "ture and compile frequently executed code regions. In Section 4"
>         uid=8_292 StaticText "we describe our approach of covering nested loops using a num-"
>         uid=8_293 StaticText "ber of individual trace trees. In Section 5 we describe our trace-"
>         uid=8_294 StaticText "compilation based speculative type specialization approach we use"
>         uid=8_295 StaticText "to generate efficient machine code from recorded bytecode traces."
>         uid=8_296 StaticText "Our implementation of a dynamic type-specializing compiler for"
>         uid=8_297 StaticText "JavaScript is described in Section 6. Related work is discussed in"
>         uid=8_298 StaticText "Section 8. In Section 7 we evaluate our dynamic compiler based on"
>         uid=8_299 StaticText "1 for (var i = 2; i < 100; ++i) {"
>         uid=8_300 StaticText "2"
>         uid=8_301 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_302 StaticText "if (!primes[i])"
>         uid=8_303 StaticText "3"
>         uid=8_304 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_305 StaticText "continue;"
>         uid=8_306 StaticText "4"
>         uid=8_307 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_308 StaticText "for (var k = i + i; i < 100; k += i)"
>         uid=8_309 StaticText "5"
>         uid=8_310 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_311 StaticText "primes[k] = false;"
>         uid=8_312 StaticText "6 }"
>         uid=8_313 StaticText "Figure 1. Sample program: sieve of Eratosthenes."
>         uid=8_314 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_315 StaticText "primes"
>         uid=8_316 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_317 StaticText "is"
>         uid=8_318 StaticText "initialized to an array of 100"
>         uid=8_319 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_320 StaticText "false"
>         uid=8_321 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_322 StaticText "values on entry to this code"
>         uid=8_323 StaticText "snippet."
>         uid=8_324 StaticText "Interpret"
>         uid=8_325 StaticText "Bytecodes"
>         uid=8_326 StaticText "Monitor"
>         uid=8_327 StaticText "Record"
>         uid=8_328 StaticText "LIR Trace"
>         uid=8_329 StaticText "Execute"
>         uid=8_330 StaticText "Compiled Trace"
>         uid=8_331 StaticText "Enter"
>         uid=8_332 StaticText "Compiled Trace"
>         uid=8_333 StaticText "Compile"

>         uid=8_335 StaticText "Leave"
>         uid=8_336 StaticText "Compiled Trace"
>         uid=8_337 StaticText "loop"
>         uid=8_338 StaticText "edge"
>         uid=8_339 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=8_340 StaticText "loop/exit"
>         uid=8_341 StaticText "abort"
>         uid=8_342 StaticText "recording"
>         uid=8_343 StaticText "finish at"
>         uid=8_344 StaticText "loop header"
>         uid=8_345 StaticText "cold/blacklisted"
>         uid=8_346 StaticText "loop/exit"
>         uid=8_347 StaticText "compiled trace"
>         uid=8_348 StaticText "ready"
>         uid=8_349 StaticText "loop edge with"
>         uid=8_350 StaticText "same types"
>         uid=8_351 StaticText "side exit to"
>         uid=8_352 StaticText "existing trace"
>         uid=8_353 StaticText "side exit,"
>         uid=8_354 StaticText "no existing trace"
>         uid=8_355 StaticText "Overhead"
>         uid=8_356 StaticText "Interpreting"
>         uid=8_357 StaticText "Native"
>         uid=8_358 StaticText "Symbol Key"
>         uid=8_359 StaticText "Figure 2."
>         uid=8_360 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_361 StaticText "State machine describing the major activities of Trace-"
>         uid=8_362 StaticText "Monkey and the conditions that cause transitions to a new activ-"
>         uid=8_363 StaticText "ity. In the dark box, TM executes JS as compiled traces. In the"
>         uid=8_364 StaticText "light gray boxes, TM executes JS in the standard interpreter. White"
>         uid=8_365 StaticText "boxes are overhead. Thus, to maximize performance, we need to"
>         uid=8_366 StaticText "maximize time spent in the darkest box and minimize time spent in"
>         uid=8_367 StaticText "the white boxes. The best case is a loop where the types at the loop"
>         uid=8_368 StaticText "edge are the same as the types on entry–then TM can stay in native"
>         uid=8_369 StaticText "code until the loop is done."
>         uid=8_370 StaticText "a set of industry benchmarks. The paper ends with conclusions in"
>         uid=8_371 StaticText "Section 9 and an outlook on future work is presented in Section 10."
>         uid=8_372 StaticText "2."
>         uid=8_373 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_374 StaticText "Overview: Example Tracing Run"
>         uid=8_375 StaticText "This section provides an overview of our system by describing"
>         uid=8_376 StaticText "how TraceMonkey executes an example program. The example"
>         uid=8_377 StaticText "program, shown in Figure 1, computes the first 100 prime numbers"
>         uid=8_378 StaticText "with nested loops. The narrative should be read along with Figure 2,"
>         uid=8_379 StaticText "which describes the activities TraceMonkey performs and when it"
>         uid=8_380 StaticText "transitions between the loops."
>         uid=8_381 StaticText "TraceMonkey always begins executing a program in the byte-"
>         uid=8_382 StaticText "code interpreter. Every loop back edge is a potential trace point."
>         uid=8_383 StaticText "When the interpreter crosses a loop edge, TraceMonkey invokes"
>         uid=8_384 StaticText "the"
>         uid=8_385 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_386 StaticText "trace monitor"
>         uid=8_387 StaticText ", which may decide to record or execute a native"
>         uid=8_388 StaticText "trace. At the start of execution, there are no compiled traces yet, so"
>         uid=8_389 StaticText "the trace monitor counts the number of times each loop back edge is"
>         uid=8_390 StaticText "executed until a loop becomes"
>         uid=8_391 StaticText " "
>         uid=8_392 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=8_393 StaticText ", currently after 2 crossings. Note"
>         uid=8_394 StaticText "that the way our loops are compiled, the loop edge is crossed before"
>         uid=8_395 StaticText "entering the loop, so the second crossing occurs immediately after"
>         uid=8_396 StaticText "the first iteration."
>         uid=8_397 StaticText "Here is the sequence of events broken down by outer loop"
>         uid=8_398 StaticText "iteration:"

>         uid=10_0 StaticText "Trace-based Just-in-Time Type Specialization for Dynamic"
>         uid=10_1 StaticText "Languages"
>         uid=10_2 StaticText "Andreas Gal"

>         uid=10_22 StaticText ", Jason Orendorff"

>         uid=10_24 StaticText ","
>         uid=10_25 StaticText "Jesse Ruderman"
>         uid=10_26 StaticText "∗"

>         uid=10_28 StaticText "#"
>         uid=10_29 StaticText ", Rick Reitmaier"
>         uid=10_30 StaticText "#"
>         uid=10_31 StaticText ", Michael Bebenita"

>         uid=10_33 StaticText ", Mason Chang"

>         uid=10_35 StaticText ", Michael Franz"
>         uid=10_36 StaticText "+"
>         uid=10_37 StaticText "Mozilla Corporation"

>         uid=10_40 StaticText "gal,brendan,shaver,danderson,dmandelin,mrbkap,graydon,bz,jorendorff,jruderman"
>         uid=10_41 StaticText "}"
>         uid=10_42 StaticText "@mozilla.com"
>         uid=10_43 StaticText "Adobe Corporation"
>         uid=10_44 StaticText "#"

>         uid=10_46 StaticText "edwsmith,rreitmai"
>         uid=10_47 StaticText "}"
>         uid=10_48 StaticText "@adobe.com"
>         uid=10_49 StaticText "Intel Corporation"
>         uid=10_50 StaticText "$"
>         uid=10_51 StaticText "{"
>         uid=10_52 StaticText "mohammad.r.haghighat"
>         uid=10_53 StaticText "}"
>         uid=10_54 StaticText "@intel.com"
>         uid=10_55 StaticText "University of California, Irvine"
>         uid=10_56 StaticText "+"
>         uid=10_57 StaticText "{"
>         uid=10_58 StaticText "mbebenit,changm,franz"
>         uid=10_59 StaticText "}"
>         uid=10_60 StaticText "@uci.edu"
>         uid=10_61 StaticText "Abstract"
>         uid=10_62 StaticText "Dynamic languages such as JavaScript are more difficult to com-"
>         uid=10_63 StaticText "pile than statically typed ones. Since no concrete type information"
>         uid=10_64 StaticText "is available, traditional compilers need to emit generic code that can"
>         uid=10_65 StaticText "handle all possible type combinations at runtime. We present an al-"
>         uid=10_66 StaticText "ternative compilation technique for dynamically-typed languages"
>         uid=10_67 StaticText "that identifies frequently executed loop traces at run-time and then"
>         uid=10_68 StaticText "generates machine code on the fly that is specialized for the ac-"
>         uid=10_69 StaticText "tual dynamic types occurring on each path through the loop. Our"
>         uid=10_70 StaticText "method provides cheap inter-procedural type specialization, and an"
>         uid=10_71 StaticText "elegant and efficient way of incrementally compiling lazily discov-"
>         uid=10_72 StaticText "ered alternative paths through nested loops. We have implemented"
>         uid=10_73 StaticText "a dynamic compiler for JavaScript based on our technique and we"
>         uid=10_74 StaticText "have measured speedups of 10x and more for certain benchmark"
>         uid=10_75 StaticText "programs."
>         uid=10_76 StaticText "Categories and Subject Descriptors"
>         uid=10_77 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_78 StaticText "D.3.4 ["
>         uid=10_79 StaticText "Programming Lan-"
>         uid=10_80 StaticText "guages"
>         uid=10_81 StaticText "]: Processors —"
>         uid=10_82 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_83 StaticText "Incremental compilers, code generation"
>         uid=10_84 StaticText "."
>         uid=10_85 StaticText "General Terms"
>         uid=10_86 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_87 StaticText "Design, Experimentation, Measurement, Perfor-"
>         uid=10_88 StaticText "mance."
>         uid=10_89 StaticText "Keywords"
>         uid=10_90 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_91 StaticText "JavaScript, just-in-time compilation, trace trees."
>         uid=10_92 StaticText "1."
>         uid=10_93 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_94 StaticText "Introduction"
>         uid=10_95 StaticText "Dynamic languages"
>         uid=10_96 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_97 StaticText "such as JavaScript, Python, and Ruby, are pop-"
>         uid=10_98 StaticText "ular since they are expressive, accessible to non-experts, and make"
>         uid=10_99 StaticText "deployment as easy as distributing a source file. They are used for"
>         uid=10_100 StaticText "small scripts as well as for complex applications. JavaScript, for"
>         uid=10_101 StaticText "example, is the de facto standard for client-side web programming"
>         uid=10_102 StaticText "Permission to make digital or hard copies of all or part of this work for personal or"
>         uid=10_103 StaticText "classroom use is granted without fee provided that copies are not made or distributed"
>         uid=10_104 StaticText "for profit or commercial advantage and that copies bear this notice and the full citation"
>         uid=10_105 StaticText "on the first page. To copy otherwise, to republish, to post on servers or to redistribute"
>         uid=10_106 StaticText "to lists, requires prior specific permission and/or a fee."
>         uid=10_107 StaticText "PLDI’09,"
>         uid=10_108 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_109 StaticText "June 15–20, 2009, Dublin, Ireland."
>         uid=10_110 StaticText "Copyright c"
>         uid=10_111 StaticText "©"
>         uid=10_112 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_113 StaticText "2009 ACM 978-1-60558-392-1/09/06. . . $5.00"
>         uid=10_114 StaticText "and is used for the application logic of browser-based productivity"
>         uid=10_115 StaticText "applications such as Google Mail, Google Docs and Zimbra Col-"
>         uid=10_116 StaticText "laboration Suite. In this domain, in order to provide a fluid user"
>         uid=10_117 StaticText "experience and enable a new generation of applications, virtual ma-"
>         uid=10_118 StaticText "chines must provide a low startup time and high performance."
>         uid=10_119 StaticText "Compilers for statically typed languages rely on type informa-"
>         uid=10_120 StaticText "tion to generate efficient machine code. In a dynamically typed pro-"
>         uid=10_121 StaticText "gramming language such as JavaScript, the types of expressions"
>         uid=10_122 StaticText "may vary at runtime. This means that the compiler can no longer"
>         uid=10_123 StaticText "easily transform operations into machine instructions that operate"
>         uid=10_124 StaticText "on one specific type. Without exact type information, the compiler"
>         uid=10_125 StaticText "must emit slower generalized machine code that can deal with all"
>         uid=10_126 StaticText "potential type combinations. While compile-time static type infer-"
>         uid=10_127 StaticText "ence might be able to gather type information to generate opti-"
>         uid=10_128 StaticText "mized machine code, traditional static analysis is very expensive"
>         uid=10_129 StaticText "and hence not well suited for the highly interactive environment of"
>         uid=10_130 StaticText "a web browser."
>         uid=10_131 StaticText "We present a trace-based compilation technique for dynamic"
>         uid=10_132 StaticText "languages that reconciles speed of compilation with excellent per-"
>         uid=10_133 StaticText "formance of the generated machine code. Our system uses a mixed-"
>         uid=10_134 StaticText "mode execution approach: the system starts running JavaScript in a"
>         uid=10_135 StaticText "fast-starting bytecode interpreter. As the program runs, the system"
>         uid=10_136 StaticText "identifies"
>         uid=10_137 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_138 StaticText "hot"
>         uid=10_139 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_140 StaticText "(frequently executed) bytecode sequences, records"
>         uid=10_141 StaticText "them, and compiles them to fast native code. We call such a se-"
>         uid=10_142 StaticText "quence of instructions a"
>         uid=10_143 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_144 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=10_145 StaticText "."
>         uid=10_146 StaticText "Unlike method-based dynamic compilers, our dynamic com-"
>         uid=10_147 StaticText "piler operates at the granularity of individual loops. This design"
>         uid=10_148 StaticText "choice is based on the expectation that programs spend most of"
>         uid=10_149 StaticText "their time in hot loops. Even in dynamically typed languages, we"
>         uid=10_150 StaticText "expect hot loops to be mostly"
>         uid=10_151 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_152 StaticText "type-stable"
>         uid=10_153 StaticText ", meaning that the types of"
>         uid=10_154 StaticText "values are invariant. (12) For example, we would expect loop coun-"
>         uid=10_155 StaticText "ters that start as integers to remain integers for all iterations. When"
>         uid=10_156 StaticText "both of these expectations hold, a trace-based compiler can cover"
>         uid=10_157 StaticText "the program execution with a small number of type-specialized, ef-"
>         uid=10_158 StaticText "ficiently compiled traces."
>         uid=10_159 StaticText "Each compiled trace covers one path through the program with"
>         uid=10_160 StaticText "one mapping of values to types. When the VM executes a compiled"
>         uid=10_161 StaticText "trace, it cannot guarantee that the same path will be followed"
>         uid=10_162 StaticText "or that the same types will occur in subsequent loop iterations."
>         uid=10_163 StaticText "Hence, recording and compiling a trace"
>         uid=10_164 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_165 StaticText "speculates"
>         uid=10_166 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_167 StaticText "that the path and"
>         uid=10_168 StaticText "typing will be exactly as they were during recording for subsequent"
>         uid=10_169 StaticText "iterations of the loop."
>         uid=10_170 StaticText "Every compiled trace contains all the"
>         uid=10_171 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_172 StaticText "guards"
>         uid=10_173 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_174 StaticText "(checks) required"
>         uid=10_175 StaticText "to validate the speculation. If one of the guards fails (if control"
>         uid=10_176 StaticText "flow is different, or a value of a different type is generated), the"
>         uid=10_177 StaticText "trace exits. If an exit becomes hot, the VM can record a"
>         uid=10_178 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_179 StaticText "branch"
>         uid=10_180 StaticText "trace"
>         uid=10_181 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_182 StaticText "starting at the exit to cover the new path. In this way, the VM"
>         uid=10_183 StaticText "records a"
>         uid=10_184 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_185 StaticText "trace tree"
>         uid=10_186 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_187 StaticText "covering all the hot paths through the loop."
>         uid=10_188 StaticText "Nested loops can be difficult to optimize for tracing VMs. In"
>         uid=10_189 StaticText "a na¨"
>         uid=10_190 StaticText "ıve implementation, inner loops would become hot first, and"
>         uid=10_191 StaticText "the VM would start tracing there. When the inner loop exits, the"
>         uid=10_192 StaticText "VM would detect that a different branch was taken. The VM would"
>         uid=10_193 StaticText "try to record a branch trace, and find that the trace reaches not the"
>         uid=10_194 StaticText "inner loop header, but the outer loop header. At this point, the VM"
>         uid=10_195 StaticText "could continue tracing until it reaches the inner loop header again,"
>         uid=10_196 StaticText "thus tracing the outer loop inside a trace tree for the inner loop."
>         uid=10_197 StaticText "But this requires tracing a copy of the outer loop for every side exit"
>         uid=10_198 StaticText "and type combination in the inner loop. In essence, this is a form"
>         uid=10_199 StaticText "of unintended tail duplication, which can easily overflow the code"
>         uid=10_200 StaticText "cache. Alternatively, the VM could simply stop tracing, and give up"
>         uid=10_201 StaticText "on ever tracing outer loops."
>         uid=10_202 StaticText "We solve the nested loop problem by recording"
>         uid=10_203 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_204 StaticText "nested trace"
>         uid=10_205 StaticText "trees"
>         uid=10_206 StaticText ". Our system traces the inner loop exactly as the na¨"
>         uid=10_207 StaticText "ıve version."
>         uid=10_208 StaticText "The system stops extending the inner tree when it reaches an outer"
>         uid=10_209 StaticText "loop, but then it starts a new trace at the outer loop header. When"
>         uid=10_210 StaticText "the outer loop reaches the inner loop header, the system tries to call"
>         uid=10_211 StaticText "the trace tree for the inner loop. If the call succeeds, the VM records"
>         uid=10_212 StaticText "the call to the inner tree as part of the outer trace and finishes"
>         uid=10_213 StaticText "the outer trace as normal. In this way, our system can trace any"
>         uid=10_214 StaticText "number of loops nested to any depth without causing excessive tail"
>         uid=10_215 StaticText "duplication."
>         uid=10_216 StaticText "These techniques allow a VM to dynamically translate a pro-"
>         uid=10_217 StaticText "gram to nested, type-specialized trace trees. Because traces can"
>         uid=10_218 StaticText "cross function call boundaries, our techniques also achieve the ef-"
>         uid=10_219 StaticText "fects of inlining. Because traces have no internal control-flow joins,"
>         uid=10_220 StaticText "they can be optimized in linear time by a simple compiler (10)."
>         uid=10_221 StaticText "Thus, our tracing VM efficiently performs the same kind of op-"
>         uid=10_222 StaticText "timizations that would require interprocedural analysis in a static"
>         uid=10_223 StaticText "optimization setting. This makes tracing an attractive and effective"
>         uid=10_224 StaticText "tool to type specialize even complex function call-rich code."
>         uid=10_225 StaticText "We implemented these techniques for an existing JavaScript in-"
>         uid=10_226 StaticText "terpreter, SpiderMonkey. We call the resulting tracing VM"
>         uid=10_227 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_228 StaticText "Trace-"
>         uid=10_229 StaticText "Monkey"
>         uid=10_230 StaticText ". TraceMonkey supports all the JavaScript features of Spi-"
>         uid=10_231 StaticText "derMonkey, with a 2x-20x speedup for traceable programs."
>         uid=10_232 StaticText "This paper makes the following contributions:"
>         uid=10_233 StaticText "•"
>         uid=10_234 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_235 StaticText "We explain an algorithm for dynamically forming trace trees to"
>         uid=10_236 StaticText "cover a program, representing nested loops as nested trace trees."
>         uid=10_237 StaticText "•"
>         uid=10_238 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_239 StaticText "We explain how to speculatively generate efficient type-specialized"
>         uid=10_240 StaticText "code for traces from dynamic language programs."
>         uid=10_241 StaticText "•"
>         uid=10_242 StaticText " "
>         uid=10_243 StaticText "We validate our tracing techniques in an implementation based"
>         uid=10_244 StaticText "on the SpiderMonkey JavaScript interpreter, achieving 2x-20x"
>         uid=10_245 StaticText "speedups on many programs."
>         uid=10_246 StaticText "The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 3 is"
>         uid=10_247 StaticText "a general overview of trace tree based compilation we use to cap-"
>         uid=10_248 StaticText "ture and compile frequently executed code regions. In Section 4"
>         uid=10_249 StaticText "we describe our approach of covering nested loops using a num-"
>         uid=10_250 StaticText "ber of individual trace trees. In Section 5 we describe our trace-"
>         uid=10_251 StaticText "compilation based speculative type specialization approach we use"
>         uid=10_252 StaticText "to generate efficient machine code from recorded bytecode traces."
>         uid=10_253 StaticText "Our implementation of a dynamic type-specializing compiler for"
>         uid=10_254 StaticText "JavaScript is described in Section 6. Related work is discussed in"
>         uid=10_255 StaticText "Section 8. In Section 7 we evaluate our dynamic compiler based on"
>         uid=10_256 StaticText "1 for (var i = 2; i < 100; ++i) {"
>         uid=10_257 StaticText "2"
>         uid=10_258 StaticText " "
